newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway finance ministry details borrowing needs.
newsitem.headline: Norway finance ministry details borrowing needs.

text.p: The Norwegian Finance ministry sought authorisation from parliament on Friday to raise new long-term domestic loans and new international loans of 50 billion crowns and 10 billion crowns respectively to cover state financing needs.
The ministry said it would present an auction calendar next month in consultation with the central bank for government bonds as well as treasury bills.
A statement said the government's gross borrowing requirement for 1997 of 38.9 billion crowns would be covered partly by domestic borrowing and partly by a reduction of the state's cash balances.
"Developments in the money and financial markets have illustrated the need for flexibility to adjust the government's borrowing to changing conditions during the year," it said.
"Therefore, the Ministry of Finance asks for authorisations to raise loans that combined exceed the borrowing requirement.
"The Ministry proposes authorisation concerning new long-term domestic loans and new international loans of 50 billion crowns and 10 billion crowns respectively," it said.
